# 2 Kings Chapter 16 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 237r–237v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_016_page_472.jpg, 2KI_016_page_473.jpg

---

**16:1** In-the-seventeenth year of-Peqach son of-Remalyahu, Achaz son of-Yotam, king of-Yehudah, became-king [malakh].

**16:2** A-son of-twenty years [ben esrim shanah] was Achaz when-he-became-king, and-sixteen years he-reigned in-Yerushalayim. And-he-did-not do the-right [ha-yashar] in-the-eyes of-YHWH his-God, like-David his-father.

**16:3** And-he-walked in-the-way [be-derekh] of-the-kings of-Yisra'el, and-also [ve-gam] his-son he-passed-through the-fire [he'evir ba-esh], according-to-the-abominations [ke-to'avot] of-the-nations whom YHWH had-dispossessed [horish] from-before the-sons of-Yisra'el.

**16:4** And-he-sacrificed [vayezabbeach] and-burned-incense [vayeqatter] on-the-high-places [ba-bamot] and-on the-hills [ha-geva'ot] and-under every green [ra'anan] tree.

**16:5** Then came-up [ya'aleh] Retsin king of-Aram and-Peqach son of-Remalyahu king of-Yisra'el to-Yerushalayim for-war [la-milchamah], and-they-besieged [vayatsuru] upon Achaz, and-they-were-not-able [lo yakhlu] to-fight [le-hillachem].

**16:6** In-that time Retsin king of-Aram returned [heshiv] Eilat to-Aram, and-drove-out [vayenashel] the-Yehudim [ha-yehudim] from-Eilat, and-Arameans [aromim] came to-Eilat and-dwelt there to this day.

**16:7** And-sent Achaz messengers [mal'akhim] to Tiglat-Pileser king of-Ashur, saying: Your-servant and-your-son [I am]; come-up and-save-me [hoshi'eni] from-the-palm of-the-king of-Aram and-from-the-palm of-the-king of-Yisra'el, the-ones-rising [ha-qomim] against-me.

**16:8** And-took Achaz the-silver and-the-gold that-was-found [ha-nimtsa] in-the-house of-YHWH and-in-the-treasuries [be-otsrot] of-the-house of-the-king, and-sent [it as] a-bribe [shochad] to-the-king of-Ashur.

**16:9** And-listened [vayishma'] to-him the-king of-Ashur, and-went-up the-king of-Ashur against Dammeseq and-captured-it [vayitpeseha], and-exiled-it [vayagleha] to-Qir, and-Retsin he-put-to-death [hemit].

**16:10** And-went the-king Achaz to-meet [liqra't] Tiglat-Pileser king of-Ashur [at] Dammeseq, and-he-saw the-altar [ha-mizbeach] that [was] in-Dammeseq, and-sent the-king Achaz to-Uriyah the-priest the-pattern [demut] of-the-altar and-its-model [tavnito] according-to-all its-workmanship [ma'asehu].

**16:11** And-built [vayiven] Uriyah the-priest the-altar; according-to-all that the-king Achaz had-sent from-Dammeseq, so did Uriyah the-priest, until the-coming of-the-king Achaz from-Dammeseq.

**16:12** And-came the-king from-Dammeseq, and-saw the-king the-altar, and-drew-near [vayiqrav] the-king to the-altar and-went-up [vaya'al] upon-it.

**16:13** And-he-burned [vayaqter] his-burnt-offering ['olato] and-his-grain-offering [minchato], and-poured-out [vayassekh] his-drink-offering [nisko], and-dashed [vayizroq] the-blood of-the-peace-offerings [dam ha-shelamim] that [were] his, upon the-altar.

**16:14** And-the-bronze altar [mizbach ha-nechoshet] that [was] before YHWH, he-brought-it-near [vayaqrev] from the-face of-the-house, from-between his-altar and-the-house of-YHWH, and-placed-it [vayitten] upon the-side [yerekh] of-the-altar northward [tsafonah].

**16:15** And-commanded the-king Achaz Uriyah the-priest, saying: Upon the-great altar [ha-mizbeach ha-gadol] burn [haqter] the-burnt-offering of-the-morning [olat ha-boqer] and-the-grain-offering of-the-evening [minchat ha-erev], and-the-burnt-offering of-the-king and-his-grain-offering, and-the-burnt-offering of-all the-people of-the-land and-their-grain-offering and-their-drink-offerings, and-all the-blood of-burnt-offering and-all the-blood of-sacrifice you-shall-dash [tizroq] upon-it. And-the-bronze altar [mizbach ha-nechoshet] shall-be for-me to-inquire [levaqer].

**16:16** And-did Uriyah the-priest according-to-all that the-king Achaz commanded.

**16:17** And-cut-off [vayeqatsets] the-king Achaz the-panels [misgerot] of-the-stands [ha-mekhonot], and-removed from-upon-them the-laver [ha-kiyyor], and-the-sea [ha-yam] he-brought-down [horid] from-upon the-bronze oxen [baqar ha-nechoshet] that [were] under-it, and-placed-it upon a-pavement of-stones [mirtsefet avanim].

**16:18** And-the-covered-way [musakh] of-the-Sabbath that they-had-built in-the-house, and-the-outer-entry [mevo'] of-the-king, he-turned [hesev] [from] the-house of-YHWH, because-of [mipney] the-king of-Ashur.

**16:19** And-the-rest of-the-acts [divrey] of-Achaz that he-did, are-they-not written in-the-scroll of-the-chronicles [sefer divrey ha-yamim] of-the-kings of-Yehudah?

**16:20** And-lay-down [vayishkav] Achaz with his-fathers, and-was-buried with his-fathers in-the-city of-David. And-became-king [vayimlokh] Chizkiyahu his-son in-his-place [tachtav].

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.3 — "passed his son through the fire":** The hiphil of *'avar* + *ba-esh* is the standard phrase for child sacrifice (cf. Deut 18:10, 2 Kgs 23:10). Ahaz is the first Judean king explicitly charged with this abomination, placing him on the level of the nations YHWH drove out. The theological irony is devastating: the king of YHWH's people practices what caused the Canaanites to lose the land.

**v.7 — "Your servant and your son":** Ahaz's self-designation as "servant and son" to Tiglath-pileser is the language of vassalage. He voluntarily submits Judah to Assyrian overlordship — politically and theologically surrendering the freedom YHWH's kingship was meant to guarantee.

**v.10 — *demut* and *tavnit*:** These are the same technical terms used for the tabernacle's design (Exod 25:9, 25:40). The narrator deliberately echoes sacred architecture language for a pagan altar copy, making Ahaz an anti-Moses.

**v.15 — "shall be for me to inquire":** The meaning of *levaqer* is disputed. It may mean "to inquire" (divination by examining sacrificial remains), "to inspect," or "to consider." If divination, Ahaz reserves the original altar for pagan practices while using the Damascus copy for YHWH worship — a complete inversion of the cult.

**v.18 — "because of the king of Ashur":** Ahaz modifies the temple's Sabbath structures and royal entrance to please the Assyrian king. Every temple modification is an act of theological capitulation — making YHWH's house conform to Assyrian expectations.

*— EMET*
